chapter_title: Concerning the Three Days and the Two Deaths
chapter_note: Despite a formulaic dialogue opening, this chapter is dominated by systematic cosmological-esoteric periodization (three “days” / two “deaths”) expressed in impersonal, structural terms (First Man descent, purification cycle, new aeon, unveiling, separation in fire). The only clear late material is the dialogue frame (¶1–3) and a moralizing/NT-colored tail in the “second death” description (¶15).

paragraphs.core_text: that there exist three great mighty days in all; and also two great and bitter deaths.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution and audience-address/application phrasing: “Once again the apostle speaks to his disciples: Happen you know, my beloved ones,” as later hagiographic/dialogue apparatus.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opens with explicit dialogue attribution (“apostle…disciples”) and direct address (“my beloved ones”), but the numbered schematic (three days / two deaths) is the underlying teaching-structure cue likely older than the frame.
Q&A frame: disciples addressing “our father” and requesting explanation; functions as editorial container rather than substrate exposition.
Pure dialogue linkage (“He speaks to them.”) with no teaching content.

paragraphs.core_text: The first day is our father, the Man. From the time when the First Man went down to the abyss of darkness and drowned in it; and the Living Spirit was sent, who went and bore him up. After the Man had ascended, the Father of Life and the Great Spirit set things in order, and the worlds above and below.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological narrative used structurally to define a temporal period; entirely internal to the Manichaean cosmic system (First Man, Living Spirit, ordering of worlds).

paragraphs.core_text: Furthermore, the glorious Ambassador came and dwelt in the ship of the day. He displayed his glorious image, and he purified the light out of all things. He walked in the heights of the heavens. Till the time when the world will be dissolved, all things destroyed, the great fire released, and the Last Statue ascends. These three deeds were begun on this first day, when they sent the First Man with his five sons.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic eschatological mechanics (purification of light, dissolution, fire, Last Statue) in the same cosmological register; no institutional/pastoral turn.

paragraphs.core_text: In contrast, [the first death] is the Darkness that mixed with the five sons of the First Man.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concise cosmological definition (Death = mixing with Darkness) wholly within the system; manuscript page marker removed per rules.

paragraphs.core_text: The second day is the time when the fathers of light, who were victorious in the struggle, will sit on their thrones in the new aeon and dwell on the new earth. And they reign in the new aeon till the Father unveils his image above them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological periodization (new aeon/new earth; enthronement; unveiling) presented as cosmic process rather than exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: The length of the sojourn in the new aeon equals the measure of the first day spent in affliction. They will reign like this and rejoice in the new aeon.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Internal temporal correspondence (measure-to-measure) extending the systematic scheme; curly-brace artifact removed.

paragraphs.core_text: The great third day [is the time] when the Father will unveil over them his image ... ... and he raises them up [ ... ] and he receives them into his hidden treasury ... and he gives [ ... ] his soul. He can pour out upon them ... his ambrosia and his sweet perfume, which takes away all affliction that they have seen with their eyes. [ ... ] fullness and a joy eternal! When his grace would sate them, he gives to them his [ ... ] and they are made anew in them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic unveiling and consummation imagery expressed as systematic eschatological mechanism (treasury, ambrosia/perfume as internal divine dispensation), without Gospel citation.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, he can summon them once more in peace and silence, and perfect their stature in same measure as his first aeons. And he sets each power in its aeon, in its dwelling-place. They will dwell in the new aeon in their aeons!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Degree/measure language (“same measure,” “each power in its aeon”) signals substrate-style ordered cosmology.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, when they dwell in their aeons, they will become rich beyond measure, for ever, beyond time. From then on they will not count that season amongst them; nor the number of the days, nor the hours, generation after generation, for ever and ever. The Father will not be hidden from them, from this time on. Rather, he has accomplished (his) unveiling to them [ ... ] he being revealed to them for ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal description of post-temporal state (beyond measure/time; unveiling permanence) continuing the internal eschatological architecture.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the three great days, [which the Father of Greatness has given number to in the reckoning].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summative closure of the three-day scheme with “reckoning/number” typical of systematic classification teaching.
Speech-transition (“that I have proclaimed to you”) functions as discourse stitching rather than substrate exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: The first death is from the time when the light fell to the Darkness, and was mixed in with the rulers of darkness; until the time when the light will become pure, and be separated from the darkness in that great fire. The remainder left behind there can build and add to that Last Statue.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic mechanics of mixture and later separation-by-fire, plus Last Statue construction—fully internal system mapping; page marker removed.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, the second death is the death in which the souls of sinful men shall die; when [they will] be stripped of the shining light that illuminates the world. And also they are separated from the living air, from which they receive [living] breath; and they are deprived of this living soul, which [ ... ] in the world; and they are separated and swept away from this Last Statue [ ... ... ] and bound on [ ... ... ] the female will become [ ... ] their torture and their affliction;
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the concluding moral/accusatory justification and “blasphemed and despised the Holy Spirit…” clause as a likely later, NT-colored moral overlay appended to a fundamentally cosmological description of the second death’s mechanism.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Base content remains cosmological (loss of light, separation from living air/breath, relation to Last Statue), but the dropped ending uses moral-judicial rhetoric and the “blasphemed…Holy Spirit” motif suggestive of later Christianized polemic.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the two deaths. The first death is temporal; [but] the second death is eternal. It is the sec[ond deat]h!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Formal definitional closure (temporal vs eternal) consistent with the chapter’s systematic twofold scheme; no institutional or citation markers.
